alerts.title: Fall armyworm outbreak (~30% of plants)
alerts.description: Drone imagery from 28 Feb shows ragged holes and frass in the leaf whorls of about 30% of plants, spreading from the eastern edge of the field.

alerts.title: Nitrogen deficiency — top-dressing window closing
alerts.description: Soil nitrogen is 9 ppm (target above 20) and the crop is at knee height, the last useful window for urea. 38 mm of rain is forecast for 2 March.

alerts.title: Harvest now: heavy rain in 48h
alerts.description: Sample plants show about 75% of pods with dark inner shells (mature). 45 mm of rain is forecast on 3 March; mature pods left in wet soil can develop aflatoxin.

alerts.title: Grey leaf spot on lower leaves
alerts.description: Drone close-ups show long, rectangular grey-brown lesions between the leaf veins on lower leaves, mostly in the wetter, low-lying half of the field.

alerts.title: Conditions favourable to black shank
alerts.description: Soil moisture has stayed above 85% with soil temperature above 25 °C for 6 days. These conditions favour black shank, a soil-borne disease. No visual symptoms have been confirmed yet.

alerts.title: Low potassium for leaf quality
alerts.description: Soil potassium is 62 ppm, below the 100 ppm target for tobacco. Low potassium reduces leaf quality and burn.

alerts.title: Early soybean rust symptoms
alerts.description: Drone images show small tan-brown spots on lower leaves in the centre of the field. Humid weather is forecast for the coming days.

alerts.title: Angular leaf spot
alerts.description: Angular brown lesions limited by the leaf veins are visible on about 15% of leaves.

alerts.title: Harvest window opens on 5 March
alerts.description: Pods are turning yellow; the harvest window is expected between 5 and 12 March. Rain on 3–4 March may slow drying.

alerts.title: Acidic soil (pH 5.0)
alerts.description: Soil pH has averaged 5.0 this season. Below 5.5, maize takes up phosphorus poorly.

alerts.title: Low phosphorus at pod set
alerts.description: Soil phosphorus is 7 ppm (target above 15). Phosphorus supports pod formation.

alerts.title: Lower leaves ripe — start priming
alerts.description: The drone colour index shows the lower leaves turning yellow-green, a sign of ripeness.

alerts.title: Groundnut rosette virus
alerts.description: Drone images show patches of stunted plants with yellow, mottled leaves. Aphids spread the virus between plants.

alerts.title: Approaching maturity (R7)
alerts.description: Most pods have turned brown; the expected harvest window is 10–20 March.

alerts.title: Urea top-dressing due in 5 days
alerts.description: The late-planted crop is approaching knee height and soil nitrogen is 14 ppm.

actions.title: Scout 20 plants in a W pattern today
actions.why: Confirm the drone finding on the ground: look for larvae and fresh frass inside the whorls. The share of infested plants decides whether spraying is needed.

actions.title: Treat the whorls early morning or late afternoon
actions.why: If more than 20% of plants are infested, apply a recommended insecticide or biopesticide into the whorls. Larvae are most exposed at these times of day.

actions.title: Re-check the field in 7 days
actions.why: Fall armyworm has several generations per season; a new wave is likely after the coming rains.

actions.title: Apply urea top-dressing today and cover it with soil
actions.why: Place the fertilizer 5–10 cm from each plant and cover it. Applied and buried before the 2 March rain, it is not washed away.

actions.title: Do not apply during the heavy rain on 2 March
actions.why: Uncovered fertilizer on wet soil is lost with the run-off.

actions.title: Check leaf colour again in 10 days
actions.why: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the lower leaves should stop moving up the plant.

actions.title: Lift groundnuts within 48 hours
actions.why: Pods are mature (inner shell dark) and 45 mm of rain is forecast on 3 March. Wet pods left in the soil develop aflatoxin.

actions.title: Dry pods on racks or tarpaulins, not on bare soil
actions.why: Contact with damp soil is the main route of aflatoxin contamination after lifting.

actions.title: Store only when kernels rattle in the shell
actions.why: Storing nuts before they are fully dry lets mould grow in the bags.

actions.title: Confirm in the field on 10 plants
actions.why: Grey leaf spot lesions are rectangular and bounded by the veins, which distinguishes them from other leaf spots.

actions.title: If lesions reach the ear leaf, consider a fungicide spray
actions.why: Protecting the ear leaf and the leaves above it protects grain filling.

actions.title: Plan a rotation with soybean or groundnut next season
actions.why: The fungus survives on maize residue; rotating crops breaks the cycle.

actions.title: Inspect stems at soil level for dark lesions
actions.why: Black shank causes black lesions at the stem base and wilting. Removing infected plants early limits spread.

actions.title: Open drainage furrows in waterlogged rows
actions.why: The pathogen moves in standing water; draining the field lowers the risk.

actions.title: Apply a chloride-free potassium fertilizer
actions.why: Tobacco needs potassium for leaf quality; chloride harms leaf burn, so potassium sulphate or nitrate are preferred.

actions.title: Check the underside of lower leaves for raised pustules
actions.why: Small raised pustules on the leaf underside confirm rust.

actions.title: If confirmed, spray a recommended fungicide before flowering ends
actions.why: Rust spreads quickly in humid weather and causes early leaf drop, reducing pod fill.

actions.title: Avoid working among the plants when leaves are wet
actions.why: The fungus spreads with rain splash and on wet hands and tools.

actions.title: Keep seed only from healthy plants
actions.why: Angular leaf spot is carried in the seed to the next season.

actions.title: Prepare tarpaulins and threshing space for 5 March
actions.why: Beans harvested at maturity and dried quickly keep their seed quality.

actions.title: Get a soil test from the district lab
actions.why: The right amount of lime depends on the soil type.

actions.title: Plan agricultural lime before next season's planting
actions.why: Lime needs a few weeks in the soil before planting to raise the pH.

actions.title: Check for dark-green, stunted plants with few pods
actions.why: These symptoms confirm that phosphorus is limiting the crop.

actions.title: Next season: phosphorus fertilizer and inoculant at planting
actions.why: Soybean needs phosphorus early; rhizobium inoculant lets the plant fix its own nitrogen.

actions.title: Prime 2–3 ripe lower leaves per plant this week
actions.why: Leaves picked at ripeness cure to a better grade.

actions.title: Check that the curing barn is ready
actions.why: Picked leaves must go into the barn on the same day.

actions.title: Uproot and bury plants with rosette symptoms
actions.why: Infected plants are a source of virus; removing them slows the spread.

actions.title: Check shoot tips for aphid colonies
actions.why: Aphids carry the virus from plant to plant.

actions.title: Next season: plant early and densely with a tolerant variety
actions.why: Early, dense crops suffer less from rosette.

actions.title: Plan harvest labour for 10 March
actions.why: Harvesting promptly at full maturity (R8) avoids losses from pod shattering.

actions.title: Harvest in the morning
actions.why: Pods are less brittle with morning dew, so fewer split open.

actions.title: Buy urea this week
actions.why: Having the fertilizer on the farm avoids missing the short top-dressing window.

actions.title: Apply at knee height, after the 3–4 March rains
actions.why: Applying to moist soil just after rain, and covering it, reduces losses.

droneCaptures.findings: Leaf damage consistent with fall armyworm on ~30% of plants, concentrated on the eastern edge.
Canopy senescence across 80% of the field, consistent with maturity.
Lesions on lower leaves in the low-lying southern half of the field.
Small tan-brown spots on lower leaves in the centre of the field.
Angular leaf lesions on ~15% of leaves; pods turning yellow.
Lower leaves turning yellow-green across the field (ripening).
Patches of stunted plants with mottled yellow leaves.
Most of the canopy has turned brown (stage R7).
